# Scientific American

> Scientific American is a premier science journalism and education platform covering research breakthroughs across physics, biology, medicine, technology, and environmental science.

Scientific American publishes in-depth articles, news analysis, and interactive content on scientific discoveries and their real-world implications. The site serves as a comprehensive resource for understanding current developments in space exploration, artificial intelligence, climate science, and biomedical research.

## Key Topics

- Space exploration
- Artificial intelligence
- Climate science
- Cosmology
- Mars exploration
- Public health
- Neuroscience
- Planetary science
- Materials science
- Scientific discovery
- COVID-19
- NASA
- Sustainability
- Medical research
- Physics

## Topic Hubs

- [Space & Physics](https://www.scientificamerican.com/space-and-physics): Space and physics topic hub covering astronomy, cosmology, and exploration
- [Technology](https://www.scientificamerican.com/technology): Technology topic hub featuring AI, aerospace, and emerging tech coverage
- [Health](https://www.scientificamerican.com/health): Health topic hub with news and articles on medical advances
- [Mind & Brain](https://www.scientificamerican.com/mind-and-brain): Neuroscience and psychology topic hub covering brain research and mental health
- [The Environment](https://www.scientificamerican.com/environment): Environmental science topic hub covering climate, ecology, and sustainability
- [Biology](https://www.scientificamerican.com/biology): Biology topic hub with research articles on life sciences and genetics
- [Math](https://www.scientificamerican.com/math): Mathematics topic hub covering statistics, topology, and mathematical puzzles
- [Chemistry](https://www.scientificamerican.com/chemistry): Chemistry topic hub featuring materials science and molecular research
- [Social Sciences](https://www.scientificamerican.com/social-sciences): Social sciences topic hub covering cultural studies and science journalism

## Featured Articles

- [Modern rocketry turns 100—and NASA says the best is yet to come](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/modern-rocketry-turns-100-and-nasa-says-the-best-is-yet-to-come): Centennial retrospective of Robert Goddard's liquid-fueled rocket legacy
- [NASA's Perseverance Mars rover discovers even older lost rivers at Jezero Crater](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/nasas-perseverance-mars-rover-discovers-even-older-lost-rivers-at-jezero): Perseverance rover ground-penetrating radar findings of ancient Mars river deltas
- [Galaxies without dark matter mystify astronomers](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/galaxies-without-dark-matter-mystify-astronomers): Exploration of bizarre dark-matter-lacking galaxies and cosmological mysteries
- [The Iran war disrupts global helium supply and artificial intelligence chipmakers](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/the-iran-war-disrupts-global-helium-supply-and-artificial-intelligence-chip): Geopolitical analysis of helium supply chain disruption affecting AI chip production
- [COVID probably killed 150,000 more people in its first two years than official U.S. tolls show](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/covid-killed-150-000-more-people-in-its-first-two-years-than-official-toll): Analysis of COVID mortality undercounting using machine learning methods
- [This overlooked organ may be more vital for longevity than scientists realized](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/this-overlooked-organ-may-be-more-vital-for-longevity-than-scientists): Thymus gland research revealing its importance for longevity and immunity
- [There might be less water on the moon than we'd hoped](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/there-might-be-less-water-on-the-moon-than-wed-hoped): Satellite data analysis revealing reduced lunar water and ice prospects
- [The math that explains why Y2K is back in fashion](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/the-math-that-explains-why-y2k-is-back-in-fashion): Mathematical modeling of fashion trend cycles and Y2K resurgence patterns
